jobs.title: Director of Engineering, Brokerage Platform
jobs.description:
Join us in building the future of finance.

Our mission is to democratize finance for all. An estimated $124 trillion of assets will be inherited by younger generations in the next two decades. The largest transfer of wealth in human history. If you’re ready to be at the epicenter of this historic cultural and financial shift, keep reading.

About the team + role

We are building an elite team, applying frontier technologies to the world's biggest financial problems. We're looking for bold thinkers. Sharp problem-solvers. Builders who are wired to make an impact. Robinhood isn't a place for complacency, it's where ambitious people do the best work of their careers. We're a high-performing, fast-moving team with ethics at the center of everything we do. Expectations are high, and so are the rewards.

The Brokerage Platform
org is the backbone of everything Robinhood trades, clears, and settles. It is the underlying infrastructure that powers every equities trade, every options contract, every event contract, and every crypto transaction that moves through our platform — and it is the foundation on which Robinhood's most important business lines are built. The org spans four deeply interconnected teams: Market Data & Symbology (the real-time and reference data layer that the entire product experience depends on), Trading Platform (core order routing, execution management, and bulk order systems), Clearing (settlement, margin, security lending, cash sweep, and the full back-office operations stack), and Brokerage Infrastructure (the platform layer that enables every product team to move faster through abstractions, reliability investments, and next-generation stack modernization). This org operates 24 hours a day around critical market functions — from market open to trade settlement — and when things go wrong, it matters.

As the Director of Engineering, Brokerage Platform
, you will lead one of Robinhood's largest and most consequential engineering organizations. You will own the technical strategy, people leadership, and delivery execution for a broad, high-stakes platform — partnering closely with a dedicated TPM and engaging deeply with trading, crypto, and active trader product teams who depend on your org every day. This is not a role for someone who manages from a distance. You will need the engineering depth to challenge technical bets, the platform mindset to drive the investments that move the business forward, and the leadership presence to build and retain a world-class team in a domain where the stakes are always high.

This role is based in our Menlo Park, CA
office, with in-person attendance expected 5
days per week.

At Robinhood, we believe in the power of in-person work to accelerate progress, spark innovation, and strengthen community. Our office experience is intentional, energizing, and designed to fully support high-performing teams.

What You’ll Do

Own the full engineering strategy and delivery for Brokerage Platform — spanning Market Data & Symbology, Trading Platform, Clearing, and Brokerage Infrastructure — setting the technical direction and ensuring the org executes with reliability and conviction
Lead and develop a large, distributed engineering organization of senior and staff-level engineers and engineering managers — building the talent, culture, and bench strength the org needs to sustain high performance over time
Drive platform investments that have direct business impact — identifying the modernization, reliability, and scalability bets worth making, building the conviction behind them, and seeing them through to measurable outcomes
Partner tightly with your TPM counterpart to manage a high volume of incoming asks from trading, crypto, active trader, and event contracts product teams — prioritizing ruthlessly and protecting engineering capacity for the work that matters most
Own the reliability and operational health of systems that run continuously around market-critical functions — ensuring the org is prepared for high-severity incidents and has the processes and tooling to resolve them fast
Engage deeply with cross-functional leadership across Robinhood — representing Brokerage Platform's roadmap, dependencies, and capabilities to product, ops, and executive stakeholders
Champion platform modernization and technical debt reduction — driving initiatives like stack rewrites, sharding, multi-region scaling, and infrastructure abstractions that unlock velocity across the entire engineering org

What You Bring

15+ years of software engineering experience, with 6+ years in engineering leadership roles — including demonstrated experience as a Director or Senior Director managing large, multi-team engineering organizations
Deep platform engineering background — you've owned and driven the technical direction of foundational backend platforms at scale, not just product features built on top of them
(big plus, though not directly required) Experience at the intersection of financial services, trading, brokerage, or adjacent high-criticality domains is a strong plus — you don't need to know all four of our sub-domains, but depth in one or two (market data, clearing, order execution, or brokerage infrastructure) is a meaningful signal
A track record of driving platform modernization bets that delivered real business outcomes — you've made the case for a large technical investment, executed it, and pointed to the result
Comfort operating in a high-severity, always-on engineering environment — you've led teams through major incidents and built the systems and culture to minimize their recurrence
Strong background with distributed systems, backend services at scale, Go or Python, and cloud infrastructure (AWS preferred)
Background from high-performance engineering organizations in fintech, trading, crypto, or large-scale consumer platforms — companies similar to Robinhood, Coinbase, SoFi, Google, or similar environments where the platform was the business is a strong plus!

Leadership expectations

Our ambitious roadmap requires a great culture shaped by exceptional leaders. Here’s what we expect from them:

Drive high performance by setting clear, focused goals, giving real-time feedback, stretching top talent, and scaling impact through focus, innovation, and tech.
Hire and retain top talent by setting a high bar, hiring only those who raise it, investing in onboarding, and addressing talent issues quickly and fairly.
Create community by connecting work to purpose, removing friction while prioritizing safety, building trust and inclusion, and leading from the front with integrity.

What We Offer

Challenging, high-impact work to grow your career.
Performance driven compensation with multipliers for outsized impact, bonus programs, equity ownership, and 401(k) matching.
Top Tier benefits to fuel your work, including 100% paid health insurance for employees with 90% coverage for dependents.
Access to the Robinhood Employee Fund that gives eligible US employees the opportunity to invest in a private employee fund that provides exposure to Robinhood Ventures funds.
Access to the best AI tools on the market and continuous AI skill-building for every employee, technical or not.
Lifestyle wallet - a highly flexible benefits spending account for wellness, learning, and more.
Employer-paid life & disability insurance, fertility benefits, and mental health benefits.
Time off to recharge including company holidays, paid time off, sick time, parental leave, and more!
Exceptional office experience with catered meals, events, and comfortable workspaces.

In addition to the base pay range listed below, this role is also eligible for bonus opportunities + equity + benefits.

Vantive is a vital organ therapy company on a mission to extend lives and expand possibilities for patients and care teams everywhere. For 70 years, our team has driven meaningful innovations in kidney care. As we build on our legacy, we are deepening our commitment to elevating the dialysis experience through digital solutions and advanced services, while looking beyond kidney care and investing in transforming vital organ therapies. Greater flexibility and efficiency in therapy administration for care teams, and longer, fuller lives for patients— that is what Vantive aspires to deliver.

We believe Vantive will not only build our leadership in the kidney care space, it will also offer meaningful work to those who join us. Join us in advancing our mission to extend lives and expand possibilities.

As the Global Software Leader for Acute Products/ Devices, this role is responsible for leading multi-site device software engineering team for Acute Care products by defining and driving software strategy and implementation and delivering to all Acute Care product lines. As the Global Device Software Leader for Acute Care product lines of Vantive, works in collaboration with commercial, systems, program management, Quality & Regulatory functional leadership teams to build and execute on product strategy, roadmaps and delivery plans.

Essential Duties And Responsibilities

Own product-line software strategy and roadmaps for device software for all acute products; aligning with business and product strategy and therapy needs.
Lead Acute global device software team, including functional managers and technical leaders.
Lead defining and implementing technology and software architecture strategy working with Acute device software leaders and in collaboration with systems leaders
Lead Acute global device software team in building execution plans and driving execution to deliver to the product roadmaps and releases across all Acute product lines.
Create, effectively communicate, and realize vision and strategy for the organization that aligns with the business and customer needs.
Establish an organization structure that ensures clear accountability and operational excellence.
Develop and mentor high-performing managers and technical leaders; build succession plans and communities of practice across global sites.

Qualifications

Significant experience in Electro-mechanical devices and device software engineering.
Understanding of global regulatory requirements for medical devices; risk and reliability concepts for development; and the need to deliver quality products and/or processes.
Significant experience leading a globally distributed team and working in a global matrix environment.
Strong team building and talent management skills, and the ability to motivate team members to achieve goals.
Proven experience in driving product specific and overall portfolio strategy, specific to software technology, in a global business.
Must possess strong knowledge of scientific/technical disciplines and solid knowledge of related disciplines such as regulatory, quality, and/or product development.
Recognized internally and externally as expert in functional area.
Must be a strategic, innovative problem solver, and have strong influencing and communication skills.
Exceptional stakeholder management and communication skills across Clinical, RA/QA, Systems, Operations, and suppliers.

Bachelor’s degree in electrical/computer/software engineering (Master’s preferred). Experience in medical devices or other safety‑critical electromechanical domains (e.g., aerospace, industrial controls, automotive) required; medical device experience strongly preferred.

jobs.title: Systems Director - Space-Based Interceptor Space Segment Engineering
jobs.description:
The Aerospace Corporation is the trusted partner to the nation’s space programs, solving the hardest problems and providing unmatched technical expertise. As the operator of a federally funded research and development center (FFRDC), we are broadly engaged across all aspects of space— delivering innovative solutions that span satellite, launch, ground, and cyber systems for defense, civil and commercial customers. When you join our team, you’ll be part of a special collection of problem solvers, thought leaders, and innovators. Join us and take your place in space.

The Defense Systems Group (DSG) provides analysis-based decision support to senior leaders on space architectures, policy and strategy, technology development, warfighter capability enablers, systems integration, defense industrial base, and threat reduction to help shape existing and future space missions across the national security space (NSS) enterprise. DSG is unique at Aerospace as it not only directly supports major customers, including the U.S. Space Force, U.S. Space Command, Air Force Material Command, and senior leadership at the Pentagon, but also provides a broad range of technical support across the national space enterprise, maintaining vertical responsibilities with customers’ portfolios as well as horizontal, matrixed responsibilities across the corporation. Additionally, DSG provides deep technical expertise to the Space Force Space Systems Command (SSC) in the conception, design, acquisition, launch and operations of satellite, launch vehicle, ground control, and range systems.

The Special Programs Division supports a broad array of Combat Power missions covering the entire threat response chain which includes the multidomain effects needed for space superiority. These programs include major system acquisitions for multiple ground and space segments, future architecture definition at the data/software/hardware levels, and research and technology for continuous evolution of space warfighting capabilities. The Space-Based Interceptor (SBI) Program Office seeks to develop and deploy a proliferated constellation of space-based interceptors capable of boost-phase engagement of adversary missiles. The SBI interceptors will employ multiple common elements that integrate with a larger layered missile defense system.

We are looking for a Systems Director - Space-Based Interceptor Space Segment Engineering
to lead the SBI Space Segment team that directly advises the government SBI Program Office on the development of the space segment of this novel missile defense capability.

The selected candidate will be required to work full-time, on-site at our facility in Huntsville, AL.

What You’ll Be Doing

Building and leading a dynamic team that provides technical expertise to the government Space-Based Interceptor Program Office (SBI PO) space segment
Exemplify Aerospace corporate values of objectivity and integrity when serving as a trusted agent to the Material Leader of the SBI space segment and senior government customers
Enabling direct reports to lead efforts to bring impactful technical expertise to the government and industry from SMEs across the corporation
Collaborating effectively with the broader layered defense architecture team and external stakeholders
Establishing a collaborative work environment that fosters a culture of innovation within the team to facilitate novel acquisition approaches for rapid capability development
Defining the Space Segment’s objectives and communicating them to subordinates, management, and interfacing matrix organizations to ensure alignment, clarity, and coordinated efforts towards achieving strategic goals and successful program execution.

What You Need To Be Successful

Minimum Requirements for Systems Director – Engineering Program Management and Systems Engineering:

Bachelor's degree in a STEM field or equivalent technical area of study
12 or more years of relevant professional or educational experience
Strong interpersonal, verbal, and written communication skills for interactions at all levels of corporate and government leadership
Proven leadership ability to operate strategically, including leading teams contributing to strategic objectives
Demonstrated ability to collaborate across organizations and manage competing priorities
Track record of delivering results through effective delegation while holding oneself accountable for results
This position requires a current and active TS/SCI security clearance, which is issued by the U.S. government. U.S citizenship is required to obtain a security clearance

How You Can Stand Out

It would be impressive if you have one or more of these:

Demonstrated experience in space systems engineering, missile defense technologies, and/or satellite operations
Proven track record of creating and leading multidisciplinary teams in high-stakes environments
Demonstration of excellent communication and interpersonal skills to effectively collaborate with government agencies, industry partners, and contractors are necessary for maintaining strong relationships and ensuring alignment among all parties
Knowledge of rigorous testing and evaluation processes, including on-orbit demonstrations and live-fire tests
Demonstrates enterprise-level perspective with prior Program Office(s) and ETG experience
Experience with novel approaches in rapid capability development and deployment
Demonstrated management skills including budgeting, staff development, and strategic planning
Knowledge of Aerospace practices and policies relevant to department leadership

We offer a competitive compensation package where you’ll be rewarded based on your performance and recognized for the value you bring to our business. Individual salaries within that range are determined through a wide variety of factors including but not limited to education, experience, knowledge and skills.

Your mission is to eliminate systemic software vulnerabilities, pioneer security paradigms for AI-driven and agentic software development, and embed autonomous controls deep into developer and cloud infrastructure workflows at hyperscale.

Google Cloud accelerates every organization’s ability to digitally transform its business and industry. We deliver enterprise-grade solutions that leverage Google’s cutting-edge technology, and tools that help developers build more sustainably. Customers in more than 200 countries and territories turn to Google Cloud as their trusted partner to enable growth and solve their most critical business problems.

We’re a team of innovators using AI at the core

If you're energized by meaningful work, love solving complex problems, and want to help modernize how legal teams operate, we’d love to meet you.

Onit is seeking a Director of Cybersecurity Engineering & Operations to lead the technical cybersecurity function across our AI-driven legal operations SaaS platforms and corporate infrastructure. Reporting to the Vice President, Compliance and Security, this highly technical leader translates the organization's cybersecurity strategy into security architecture, engineering capabilities, and security operations that protect our products, cloud environments, employees, and corporate systems. The Director leads a cybersecurity manager and a team of security engineers and operations professionals, and partners closely with Cloud Engineering, Product Engineering, IT, and Compliance to reduce risk while enabling the company to build and operate securely.

Key Responsibilities

Develop and execute the cybersecurity engineering and operations strategy with the VP, Compliance and Security, translating risk and business priorities into technical roadmaps, architecture standards, and measurable outcomes (e.g., remediation performance, control coverage, incident response effectiveness, attack surface and posture trends).
Lead the design and continuous improvement of security controls and guardrails across AWS and corporate environments, including cloud identity, network, workload, container/Kubernetes, and data protections, with security automation delivered as code (Terraform, Python, CI/CD, policy-as-code).
Own technical security operations and incident response: detection, investigation, containment, eradication, and recovery; maintain and exercise IR plans, playbooks, and runbooks; build automated detection and response workflows across SIEM, SOAR, EDR, and cloud-native tooling; and coordinate executive, legal, and regulatory escalation with the VP.
Own the vulnerability and exposure management program across applications, cloud, endpoints, and external attack surfaces, setting risk-based remediation SLAs and prioritizing by exploitability, exposure, and business impact while driving root-cause fixes for systemic weaknesses.
Provide security leadership for Microsoft 365 and Entra ID (MFA, Conditional Access, privileged identity management, Just-In-Time access), corporate endpoint and email security, and for application and product security across the SDLC, including SAST/DAST/SCA, SBOMs, API security, threat modeling, a security champions program, and AI-enabled applications and integrations.
Lead, mentor, and develop the cybersecurity manager, engineers, and security operations staff; define team structure, career paths, and operating processes that scale; manage security vendors, penetration testing, and managed security services; and serve as senior technical security advisor to Engineering, IT, Product, and executive leadership.

Required Skills

10+ years of progressive cybersecurity experience, including 5+ years in security leadership or management roles leading security engineering, security operations, or cloud security functions, with experience managing managers and technical teams.
Deep expertise securing cloud-native enterprise SaaS applications, with strong hands-on AWS security experience (IAM, VPC, EC2, RDS, S3, EKS/ECS, logging, monitoring) and strong knowledge of Linux, networking, containers, and Kubernetes.
Strong experience with security technologies including SIEM, EDR, CSPM, vulnerability management, WAF, and security monitoring platforms, and demonstrated experience building or improving incident detection and response programs.
Experience securing Microsoft 365 and Entra ID environments (identity protection, MFA, Conditional Access, privileged identity management, access governance) and implementing privileged access management and Just-In-Time access architectures.
Strong understanding of application and API security (SAST, DAST, SCA, SBOMs, secrets management, authentication/authorization) and experience with security automation and scripting using Python, Bash, Terraform, APIs, and CI/CD platforms, including Infrastructure-as-Code security and policy-as-code guardrails.
Hands-on AI tool proficiency: experience using AI tools and LLM-based assistants in security work (e.g., AI-assisted alert triage, investigation, detection engineering, and automation), including crafting effective prompts, evaluating output accuracy, and integrating AI into security workflows. Experience securing AI-enabled applications, LLM integrations, and APIs is a plus.
Ability to communicate complex cybersecurity risks to engineering leaders, executives, and non-technical stakeholders, and to balance risk reduction with business objectives and engineering velocity.
Preferred: experience with multi-tenant SaaS security, CrowdStrike, Cloudflare (WAF and Zero Trust), DevSecOps, and offensive security or red-team programs; familiarity with SOC 2, ISO 27001, NIST, or FedRAMP technical controls; and certifications such as CISSP, CCSP, AWS Security Specialty, or GIAC.

Three medical plan options, plus dental and vision, so you can choose what fits best. Employees on our HDHP plan also receive employer contribution to the HSA.

100% employer-paid life and disability insurance.

Additional Coverage Options:
Voluntary benefits including hospital indemnity, critical illness, accident, and even pet insurance.

Healthcare FSA, HSA, and dependent care FSA.

Community Engagement:
One paid volunteer day each year to give back to the community.

Location
On-site role based out of Twinsburg, OH; Cincinnati, OH; or Somerset, NJ. Candidates must currently live within a commutable distance of one of these locations or be willing to relocate.

$160,000 - $180,000 base compensation. This range represents a good faith estimate of the expected base salary for this position. The Senior Director, Infrastructure & Operations is responsible for leading the teams that support the company’s enterprise technology foundation, including infrastructure, network, cloud, data center, identity and access management, endpoint computing, collaboration platforms, service desk operations, and infrastructure security and risk support.

This role supports a national, highly distributed environment across branch locations, manufacturing facilities, corporate offices, and data centers. The Senior Director will ensure critical technology services remain stable, secure, scalable, resilient, and aligned with business needs.

The ideal candidate is an experienced infrastructure and operations leader who began their career in a hands-on technical role and progressed into senior leadership. This individual will partner closely with executives and technical teams, assess current operations, build practical roadmaps, improve service levels, develop talent, strengthen accountability, and drive continuous improvement across the organization.

Set the strategic direction for enterprise infrastructure and operations, developing roadmaps that support business growth, scalability, security, and evolving business needs while evaluating current platforms, identifying gaps, prioritizing improvements, and establishing consistent operational standards, processes, and expectations.
Serve as a trusted advisor to executive leadership on infrastructure decisions, investments, and risks, partnering with enterprise technology leadership to ensure infrastructure, identity, and endpoint platforms are prepared to support AI tools and services across the organization.
Participate in enterprise AI governance, evaluating the infrastructure, security, and data implications of new AI tools and technologies entering the environment.

IT Operations

Lead day-to-day enterprise infrastructure and support operations, creating consistency in incident, change, problem, and outage management while improving service quality, responsiveness, and the overall user experience.

Network, Cloud & Infrastructure Services

Track and report key metrics including infrastructure availability, SLA attainment, MTTR, MTTD, First Contact Resolution, change success rates, incident trends, vulnerability remediation, endpoint compliance, and customer satisfaction.
Present operational performance, trends, risks, and improvement plans to executive leadership, using data and measurable outcomes to identify improvement opportunities, strengthen accountability, and drive decisions based on business impact.

Team Leadership

Lead, coach, develop, recruit, and retain a strong team of infrastructure and operations professionals, establishing clear priorities, expectations, and accountability while building future leaders.
Foster a culture of ownership, open communication, follow-through, and accountability across the organization.

Business Partnership & Vendor Management

Build strong relationships with executives, business leaders, and operational stakeholders, translating technical concepts into clear business terms and partnering effectively across the organization.

You'll partner closely with Product, Architecture, and Engineering leaders to deliver innovative platform capabilities, improve engineering practices, and accelerate the transformation of legacy applications into modern cloud-native services.

Lead and develop high-performing engineering teams responsible for delivering scalable, secure, and reliable digital platform capabilities.
Drive modernization initiatives by transforming legacy applications into cloud-native solutions using modern architectural patterns, including APIs, microservices, and event-driven design.

Provide technical leadership by reviewing solution designs, guiding architectural decisions, mitigating risks, and promoting scalable, maintainable solutions.
Partner with Product Management, Architecture, UX, Infrastructure, Security, and other stakeholders to deliver business priorities while balancing speed, quality, and technical debt.
Ensure platform reliability and operational excellence through proactive monitoring, incident management, performance optimization, and continuous improvement.
Foster a culture of accountability, collaboration, innovation, and continuous learning across engineering teams.
Recruit, mentor, and retain top engineering talent while supporting career development, performance management, and succession planning.
Coach engineering managers, technical leads, and software engineers to strengthen technical capability and leadership across the organization.
Drive engineering excellence by improving delivery predictability, development velocity, software quality, and customer outcomes.
Lead teams through organizational and technology transformation initiatives, helping accelerate Ferguson's digital modernization journey.

Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Information Technology, or a related field, or equivalent work experience.

Job Details

About Salesforce

Salesforce is the #1 AI CRM, where humans with agents drive customer success together. Here, ambition meets action. Tech meets trust. And innovation isn’t a buzzword — it’s a way of life. The world of work as we know it is changing and we're looking for Trailblazers who are passionate about bettering business and the world through AI, driving innovation, and keeping Salesforce's core values at the heart of it all.

Ready to level-up your career at the company leading workforce transformation in the agentic era? You’re in the right place! Agentforce is the future of AI, and you are the future of Salesforce.

Slack is looking for an Engineering Manager on the Core Services engineering team. The purpose of this role is to keep Slack working seamlessly at massive scale — it's the infrastructure that keeps Slack feeling lightning fast. This person will be a steward of some of the most critical, high-throughput systems at Slack — the kind of work where doing it well means millions of users, at the world’s most important and interesting companies, never experience a hiccup.

About The Opportunity

We operate at tremendous scale with systems that process millions of events per second. Our team maintains and builds performant services that include:

Edge Caches
Realtime Services
Enterprise Key Management (EKM)
International Data Residency (IDR)
Image Uploads, Downloads, and Proxying

We've done our job correctly when none of our users think about us, much like a vital utility. We don't typically ship new user-facing features, but rather ensure our systems are exceptionally performant, highly available, reliable, and scalable. In other words, we make Slack work seamlessly. Slack's backend services are written in Go and Java, and Slack's API is built on PHP/Hack.

The Core Services Team

We are a team building critical services that enable Slack to scale for our largest customers. Our edge caches power the most latency-critical queries for our largest entities today, serving approximately 35% of all Slack API traffic. Our Realtime Services (RTS) power Slack's core messaging stack — running 10 services, 4 of which are mission-critical Tier 0 services — ensuring that messages, presence, and real-time events are delivered reliably at scale. We also own services that power Slack's Enterprise Key Management and International Data Residency features, enabling Slack to win and retain enterprise and government customers with strict compliance requirements (FedRAMP/NIST).

We have a strong commitment to quality and understand that simplicity and reliability are the foundations of our work.

We are actively building the future of edge services at Slack, so we can support a growing number of globally distributed customers with their compliance requirements with minimal latency.

What You'll Be Doing

Owning the technical direction and roadmap across the Core Services portfolio: Edge Caches, Realtime Services, Enterprise Key Management, International Data Residency, and Image Proxying and Uploads. You’ll have large footprint and the opportunity to drive major impact. And you'll decide what to invest in now, what to sequence later, and what to decline — balancing reliability, migration, and new capability work.
Leading a multi-system migration of Flannel to Loom, our next-generation edge cache, while keeping the current systems running at full reliability for millions of users. You'll drive the team to ship new capabilities without introducing risk to infrastructure that people depend on daily.
Driving delivery and execution while maintaining reliability as a top priority, including sprint planning, product launches, incident follow-ups, operational sustainability analyses, and building the technical case for investment with leadership. You'll ensure the team doesn't trade reliability for velocity, but is always high-performing.
Owning on-call operations and incident management for Tier 0 services. You'll manage on-call rotations across partnering teams, triage production issues, lead incident response for your services, and drive improvements to runbooks, alerting, and operational tooling.
Partnering cross-functionally with Product, Sales, Compliance, Security, AWS, and other infrastructure teams on dependencies, timelines, and risks. You'll be the shortest path to solutions — whether it's unblocking a compliance audit for South Korea, coordinating IDR region launches with Sales and AWS, or negotiating priorities with partner teams for shared work.
Representing your team's work in leadership reviews, quarterly and annual planning, and executive forums. You'll build compelling business-and-technical cases for your team's investments and tell your leadership what's really going on early enough that nothing becomes a fire drill.
Building and maintaining a high-trust team culture where engineers do impactful work and grow. You'll hire well, manage performance with fairness and transparency, mentor emerging technical leaders, and celebrate your team's wins.
Managing cost and capacity for services that run at massive scale, working with finance on AWS spend trends, exec-approved budget increases, and cost-saving initiatives like the Loom migration (projected $1-2M savings).
Driving the team to adopt AI development tooling for maximum impact, while maintaining engineering rigor and quality for critical infrastructure.

You're Our Person If

You've led engineering teams for 5+ years building and operating high-scale, high-availability backend infrastructure or distributed systems.
You have strong software engineering fundamentals with previous experience as a Senior+ backend engineer, with enough depth to be credible in architecture discussions about caching, distributed systems, observability and reliability best practices, and system design — and to build SME knowledge in a new area fast.
You have a history of managing Tier 0 / Tier 1 services where uptime matters deeply, including owning on-call rotations, leading incident response, and driving operational improvements.
You have experience with realtime messaging systems or event-driven architectures at scale — presence, message delivery, pub/sub, or similar systems where latency and reliability directly impact user experience.
You have experience leading multi-quarter migration or platform evolution projects while simultaneously keeping existing systems reliable.
You've managed teams through prioritization trade-offs — weighing reliability vs. feature work vs. cost vs. compliance — and can articulate those decisions to both engineers and executives.
You have experience partnering with cross-functional stakeholders (Product, Sales, Compliance, Security, Infrastructure) to turn business requirements into engineering plans.
You understand how to build a high-performing team culture: hiring, performance management, retention of top performers, and growing new technical leaders.
You have experience managing engineers across multiple time zones, with an async rhythm that doesn't depend on overlap hours.
An understanding of how and where AI software development tooling can be deployed for maximum team impact.

Even Better If

You have experience with the Go and/or Java programming language at scale.
Experience with AWS infrastructure, including multi-region architectures.
Experience with Kubernetes and container-based deployments.
Experience working within highly regulated environments where an understanding of FedRAMP/NIST frameworks was essential.
Experience with Enterprise Key Management, data residency, or compliance-driven infrastructure.
You've managed teams responsible for Edge Caching, CDN, or API gateway systems.
You've led teams through system deprecation and migration while maintaining service reliability.

Unleash Your Potential

When you join Salesforce, you’ll be limitless in all areas of your life. Our benefits and resources support you to find balance and be your best , and our AI agents accelerate your impact so you can do your best . Together, we’ll bring the power of Agentforce to organizations of all sizes and deliver amazing experiences that customers love. Apply today to not only shape the future — but to redefine what’s possible — for yourself, for AI, and the world.

jobs.description:
Description

Senior Software Development Manager, FAIM Evaluations.

Amazon Advertising is building toward a future where an advertiser specifies a few marketing parameters (budget, success definition, which products to promote) and a set of AI agents handles the rest. The Full Funnel Agentic Intelligence and Models (FAIM) organization owns that bet: the Ads Nova agent, the Ads Nova model it reasons with, and the agent infrastructure, learning environments, and evaluations that connect the two. We are looking for a Senior Software Development Manager to found and lead the FAIM Evaluations team. You will report directly to the Vice President of Full Funnel Agentic Intelligence and Models and own how the entire organization answers one question: is this actually good at advertising?

This is a ground-up build. Evaluation today lives inside individual model and agent teams, measured task by task. You will create the standalone engineering team that turns it into a shared, rigorous system spanning the Ads Nova model, the Ads Nova agent, and the internal agent that serves our Sales, Services, and Operations teams. No inherited harness, no pattern to follow, and a direct line to the VP who sponsors the work.

What we're building

An advertising benchmark: a representative set of real advertising tasks, organized by domain and difficulty, from single-step questions through multi-step analysis to long-horizon strategic work, each with structured criteria for what a correct end-to-end response looks like

Evaluation infrastructure that scores models and agents deterministically against that benchmark, compares Ads Nova to frontier models on the tasks that matter to advertisers, and gives every science and product team in FAIM the same yardstick

Rubrics and task environments built to serve double duty: scoring quality today and producing the reward signal that trains the next version of the model

An expert-in-the-loop program that captures how experienced advertising practitioners actually work and encodes that judgment into criteria a machine can grade against

A capability map, derived from benchmark results, that tells FAIM where the model and agent stand and what to train next

Key job responsibilities

Found and lead a standalone team of roughly 10-12: software engineers plus a product manager and a technical program manager; you will hire most of them

Own the technical vision and roadmap for FAIM evaluations end to end: task taxonomy, rubric design, environment construction, scoring, benchmark versioning, and the separation between what we evaluate on and what we train on

Build for the whole org, not one product: your team evaluates the Ads Nova model, the Ads Nova agent, and the internal agent, and you participate in the planning and reviews for all three

Partner with applied scientists across FAIM to turn evaluation criteria into training signal for reinforcement learning, and to make sure what we measure is what we optimize

Run the domain-expert program: source advertising practitioners, define the annotation and calibration process, and hold the quality bar on inter-rater agreement

Set the evaluation standard for the organization and hold the line on it; where good internal assets already exist, adopt them rather than rebuild

Publish results leadership and partner teams trust, and own the cadence for re-scoring as models, agents, and tasks evolve

Represent evaluations in VP-level reviews, annual planning, and cross-org discussions on model and agent quality

We're looking for a leader who brings

10+ years of engineering experience and 5+ years managing engineering teams, including building a team from a small core

A track record delivering evaluation systems, benchmarks, or data-quality programs for machine learning models, ideally large language models or agentic systems

Working fluency in how modern models are trained and improved (supervised fine-tuning, reinforcement learning from rubric or verifier signal) and what makes an eval useful as a training asset rather than only a scorecard

Judgment about measurement: when all-or-nothing grading beats partial credit, how to find ambiguous criteria through grader disagreement

Experience running expert-annotation or labeling programs with external partners, including quality control at scale

The ability to operate in ambiguity: turn "is it good at advertising" into a concrete, scored, versioned asset with minimal scoping help

Comfort working as the engineering counterpart to scientists you do not manage, and the influence to get model, agent, and product teams onto one yardstick

Advertising domain knowledge, or the curiosity and speed to build it by working closely with practitioners

Experience with Amazon Bedrock, agent frameworks, and tool-use protocols (MCP) is a plus

10+ years of engineering experience
5+ years of engineering team management experience
10+ years of planning, designing, developing and delivering consumer software experience
Experience partnering with product or program management teams
Experience managing multiple concurrent programs, projects and development teams in an Agile environment
10+ years of software development experience
Bachelor's degree in computer science, computer engineering, or related technical field
Experience designing, building, operating, and managing large-scale distributed systems or web services
Experience with software development in a team, and a track record of shipping software on time

We’re building the system that replaces the many tools owners use to run their business.

Most small business software makes owners do the work to get what they want: sales growth and profit growth. Owner does the work for them agentically.

Once we nail the solution for restaurants – we’ll scale it into every other local business type.

In the future we envision, tens of millions of local business owners will use our technology to succeed in the digital age.

jobs.description:
About Nscale

At Nscale, we are building the infrastructure for the AI revolution. Nscale is developing cutting-edge, sovereign generative AI solutions powered by a new generation of high-performance, sustainable data centers and GPUs built specifically for AI workloads.

The rapid growth of artificial intelligence is driving unprecedented global demand for compute and GPU infrastructure. Positioned at the heart of this transformation, Nscale is delivering the platforms that will enable the next decade of innovation.

Working closely with the world's most advanced AI technology providers, including Microsoft and NVIDIA, Nscale integrates next-generation compute hardware and Next GPU clusters across both partner and self-delivered facilities. This is a unique opportunity to join Nscale's journey, play a pivotal role in delivering transformative AI infrastructure, and help shape a company designed to scale rapidly across North America, Europe, and beyond.

About the Role

We are hiring a Director, Pipeline Engineering to own the engineering of the natural gas transmission pipelines that fuel Nscale's generation campuses, from upstream interconnect to plant fence.

Nscale's Power and Energy group develops behind-the-meter generation colocated with our data center campuses: large reciprocating engine fleets served by dedicated, large-diameter gas transmission pipelines moving hundreds of millions of cubic feet per day. These are not ordinary laterals. The pipeline is also the storage: line pack is the operating inventory that buffers nominations against engine demand, pressure is governed by that inventory balance, and the design of overpressure protection, regulation, and system controls determines whether gigawatts of compute stay online. Much of this work is closer to process engineering than to conventional pipeline design, and this role owns it.

This is a senior, hands-on technical leadership role built for someone who runs independently, with full delegated ownership of the pipeline scope. You will establish the design basis for our pipelines and demonstrate how it ties to our downstream commitments (engine demand, swing, and availability), drive the engineering through hydraulic design, controls philosophy, and construction, and technically manage the third-party engineering firms and pipeline construction contractors doing the work. Lines are in delivery today and new lines will follow, so the role owns both the systems being built now and the reference engineering for what comes next.

You will sit within the Power and Energy technology organization, working alongside the generation engineering and commissioning teams that depend on the gas you deliver. You will be the owner's technical authority on the pipeline scope, directing the work of consultants and contractors rather than simply accepting it, and resolving the design questions where standard midstream practice does not account for a single customer whose demand can swing with AI workloads. As the accountable leader for pipeline engineering at Nscale, you will set the design basis, establish the standards, and represent Nscale's position with EPC partners, upstream operators, and executives, and you will be expected to do so from day one.

Location:
Houston, TX (remote considered within the US, with regular site and vendor travel)

What You'll Be Doing

Pipeline system engineering and design basis

Own the design basis for Nscale's gas transmission pipelines: hydraulic design, MAOP and pressure regime, line pack and inventory strategy, routing and sizing philosophy, and expansion provisions for future lines.
Perform and direct steady-state and transient hydraulic modeling of the pipeline systems, and own the models as living engineering assets that answer real operating questions: inventory swing, survival time on line pack, ramp response, and curtailment scenarios.
Demonstrate explicitly how the pipeline design basis supports downstream commitments: engine fleet demand and turndown, campus availability requirements, and the nominations-versus-consumption balance that governs system pressure.
Evaluate gas storage and supply resilience options, including line pack utilization, interconnect diversity, and cross-connection strategies between lines, with clear analysis of the risk each option carries.

Process and controls engineering

Own the overpressure protection philosophy across the pipeline systems: regulation, monitor, slam-shut, and relief selection, justified against reliability requirements, industry practice, and regulatory obligations rather than habit.
Define the control philosophy at interconnects, letdown stations, and plant interfaces: pressure versus flow control, control interactions with upstream operators' facilities, and the measurement and SCADA provisions needed to run the system on inventory.
Apply process safety discipline to the pipeline scope: lead and support HAZOPs and design reviews, own the closure of actions, and carry management of change through design and construction.
Engineer the interface into the plant fuel gas systems, coordinating conditioning, letdown, and protection philosophies so pipeline and plant behave as one system.

Regulatory compliance and integrity

Own compliance of the pipeline designs with 49 CFR Part 192 and the applicable ASME B31 codes, including the code boundaries between jurisdictional pipeline and plant piping.
Establish material, welding, and construction specifications, class location and MAOP documentation, and the records discipline that a traceable, verifiable, and complete basis requires.
Lay the foundation for integrity management: baseline assessment planning, pigging and inspection provisions, and mainline valve philosophy, including remote actuation and its treatment in availability analysis.
Support commissioning and first gas: purge and pack planning, energization of the measurement and control systems, and readiness reviews in partnership with the commissioning and startup organization.

Third-party technical management

Technically manage the engineering consultants supporting the pipeline scope: set the design basis they work to, review and challenge their deliverables, and integrate their output into a coherent whole.
Direct pipeline construction contractors on technical matters: specification compliance, field queries, deviation dispositions, and as-built reconciliation.
Own the technical interface with upstream pipeline operators and interconnect counterparties: metering station design, control coordination, nominations behavior, and the operating agreements' technical exhibits.
Hold third parties to disciplined engineering, testing, and documentation, and know when their standard answer is not good enough for this application.
Own the scope, schedule, and budget of third-party pipeline engineering: define consultant scopes of work, review and recommend change orders and addenda, and hold firms accountable to their commitments.

Standards and cross-functional leadership

Develop Nscale's engineering standards, specifications, and reference designs for gas pipelines, so each new line builds on the last instead of starting over.
Coordinate with generation engineering on fuel gas requirements, with permitting and land teams on routing and regulatory strategy, and with commercial teams on gas supply and transportation arrangements.
Build and lead the internal pipeline engineering function, directing specialist consultants today and hiring and developing a team as the portfolio scales.
Communicate complex pipeline and process issues clearly to project leadership and executives, with honest assessments of risk and readiness, and represent Nscale's pipeline scope in design basis alignment with EPC partners, upstream operators, and customers.

About You

15+ years of natural gas pipeline engineering experience across design, construction, and operations, with significant time in a lead or owner's engineer role on transmission systems, including senior accountability for the outcome of major transmission projects.

VERRA MOBILITY

SOFTWARE ENGINEERING

Director, Software Engineering

Who We Are...

Verra Mobility is a global leader in smart mobility. We develop technology-enabled solutions that help the world move safely and easily. We are fostering the development of safe cities, working with police departments and municipalities to install over 4,000 red-light, speed, and school bus stop arm safety cameras across North America. We are also creating smart roadways, serving the world's largest commercial fleets and rental car companies to manage tolling transactions and violations for over 8.5 million vehicles. And we are a leading provider of connected systems, processing nearly 165 million transactions each year across 50+ individual tolling authorities.

Culture

Verra Mobility Corporation is a dynamic, entrepreneurial company that operates with a people-first philosophy and approach. The company lives by its core values—Do What’s Right, Choose Courage Over Comfort, Win Together, and Own It—in everything it does for its customers and team members. The company seeks to grow, both organically and through acquisition, to continue to be the undisputed market leader with a bias for action, customer focus, teamwork, drive for results, and commitment to excellence.

Position Overview

The Director, Software Engineering is the technical subject matter expert and engineering leader for the Platform portfolio, reporting to the SVP, Software Engineering and owning technology strategy and end to end delivery outcomes for the portfolio’s squads. This role requires deep domain expertise in the portfolio’s problem space, current fluency across modern engineering practices, and the operating pace expected of a modern software organization.

You will partner with the external Product Portfolio Director on product vision, engage directly with partner and customer technical teams on architecture and integration, and be responsible for evaluating and developing the technical leadership within your portfolio. Your work will determine how quickly a steady state organization can move, and whether the portfolio’s platforms are built once and reused, or rebuilt every time a new need arises.

Essential Responsibilities

Technical Strategy & Architecture

Own Portfolio Technology Strategy: Define technology strategy and end to end delivery outcomes for the portfolio’s squads, maintaining deep domain expertise in the portfolio’s problem space and current fluency in the broader technology and competitive landscape, including modern AI and machine learning solution categories.
Identify Reuse Before Rebuild: Identify where shared platform capabilities can be extended or reused rather than rebuilt, partnering with the Platform team and Senior Enterprise Architect to avoid duplicated effort.
Maintain Domain and Integration Fluency: Maintain a working view of service boundaries, API contracts, and event driven or asynchronous processing patterns across the portfolio, recognizing a fragile integration or a duplicative build before it hardens into a dependency other teams must unwind.

Delivery, Migration & Operational Ownership

Own End to End Delivery: Own predictable, high quality delivery across the portfolio’s squads, including roadmap commitments, release readiness, budget adherence, and operational stability.
Raise Delivery Pace: Change how quickly a steady state organization moves, accelerating delivery pace and urgency within an existing, already staffed organization.
Lead Platform Migrations: Lead live system migrations and legacy platform transitions, including cutover sequencing, data reconciliation, and rollback planning, as clients and workloads move off legacy platforms and onto current ones.
Govern Data & Security: Apply data architecture and governance principles, including data lineage and stewardship for shared or regulated datasets, and ensure the portfolio’s systems meet security and compliance expectations for multi tenant, transaction heavy systems operating across multiple jurisdictions.
Own Bid & Contract Review: Own final review and approval of new contracts and bids for the Platform portfolio, building on the Manager’s initial technical and compliance review to confirm proposed work is achievable within existing governance, architectural, and delivery constraints before commitments are made.

Talent & Organizational Leadership

Develop Technical Leaders: Personally assess whether direct and indirect reports are functioning above or below the title held, and act on that assessment through coaching, role redefinition, or personnel change.
Ensure Technical Succession: Treat technical succession as a stated priority, so no portfolio depends on a single person’s tenure for its technical continuity.
Partner Across the Enterprise: Partner closely with the Portfolio Architect as the technical decision making pair for the portfolio, coordinate with peer Directors and the Senior Enterprise Architect to keep cross portfolio integrations coherent, and align regularly with the Product Portfolio Director function to reconcile product vision and technical reality.

We’re Looking For a Technical Leader With a Proven Track Record Of Owning Outcomes, Modernizing Platforms, And Raising Delivery Pace At Scale. The Ideal Candidate Will Bring The Following Capabilities

Portfolio Technology Strategy

Ability to define and sustain a coherent technology strategy across a multi squad portfolio, balancing standardization with legitimate portfolio specific divergence.

Architecture & Integration Judgment

Fluency in domain boundaries, API contract design, and event driven or asynchronous processing patterns, sufficient to judge whether a proposed integration is a durable seam or a future liability.

Migration & Modernization Leadership

Demonstrated experience leading a live system migration or legacy platform transition, including cutover sequencing, data reconciliation, and rollback planning.

Data & Governance Fluency

Working knowledge of data architecture, data lineage, and the security and compliance considerations relevant to multi tenant, transaction heavy systems.

Talent Development & Succession

Track record of assessing, coaching, and developing technical leaders, including making difficult talent calls when needed.

Executive & Partner Communication

Technical credibility sufficient to lead architecture and technology discussions directly with partner and customer engineering teams, and to evaluate a vendor pitch or build proposal critically.

Bid & Contract Ownership

Ability to review and approve contracts and bids for technical, architectural, and delivery feasibility, ensuring commitments are not made against a portfolio that cannot support them.

Qualifications

Experience: 10+ years in software engineering delivering enterprise systems, including 5+ years leading multiple teams or squads through Managers and Tech Leads. Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or equivalent experience required.
Technical Fluency: Current fluency with modern engineering stacks relevant to the portfolio, including .NET/C#, Java, SQL, modern web frameworks, REST and GraphQL APIs, microservices, cloud platforms, and event driven or asynchronous processing patterns such as message queues and event streaming.
Migration & Legacy Transition: Demonstrated experience leading a live system migration or legacy platform transition, including cutover sequencing, data reconciliation, and rollback planning.

new_jobs.title: Director, Pipeline Engineering
new_jobs.description:
About Nscale

At Nscale, we are building the infrastructure for the AI revolution. Nscale is developing cutting-edge, sovereign generative AI solutions powered by a new generation of high-performance, sustainable data centers and GPUs built specifically for AI workloads.

The rapid growth of artificial intelligence is driving unprecedented global demand for compute and GPU infrastructure. Positioned at the heart of this transformation, Nscale is delivering the platforms that will enable the next decade of innovation.

Working closely with the world's most advanced AI technology providers, including Microsoft and NVIDIA, Nscale integrates next-generation compute hardware and Next GPU clusters across both partner and self-delivered facilities. This is a unique opportunity to join Nscale's journey, play a pivotal role in delivering transformative AI infrastructure, and help shape a company designed to scale rapidly across North America, Europe, and beyond.

About the Role

We are hiring a Director, Pipeline Engineering to own the engineering of the natural gas transmission pipelines that fuel Nscale's generation campuses, from upstream interconnect to plant fence.

Nscale's Power and Energy group develops behind-the-meter generation colocated with our data center campuses: large reciprocating engine fleets served by dedicated, large-diameter gas transmission pipelines moving hundreds of millions of cubic feet per day. These are not ordinary laterals. The pipeline is also the storage: line pack is the operating inventory that buffers nominations against engine demand, pressure is governed by that inventory balance, and the design of overpressure protection, regulation, and system controls determines whether gigawatts of compute stay online. Much of this work is closer to process engineering than to conventional pipeline design, and this role owns it.

This is a senior, hands-on technical leadership role built for someone who runs independently, with full delegated ownership of the pipeline scope. You will establish the design basis for our pipelines and demonstrate how it ties to our downstream commitments (engine demand, swing, and availability), drive the engineering through hydraulic design, controls philosophy, and construction, and technically manage the third-party engineering firms and pipeline construction contractors doing the work. Lines are in delivery today and new lines will follow, so the role owns both the systems being built now and the reference engineering for what comes next.

You will sit within the Power and Energy technology organization, working alongside the generation engineering and commissioning teams that depend on the gas you deliver. You will be the owner's technical authority on the pipeline scope, directing the work of consultants and contractors rather than simply accepting it, and resolving the design questions where standard midstream practice does not account for a single customer whose demand can swing with AI workloads. As the accountable leader for pipeline engineering at Nscale, you will set the design basis, establish the standards, and represent Nscale's position with EPC partners, upstream operators, and executives, and you will be expected to do so from day one.

Location:
Houston, TX (remote considered within the US, with regular site and vendor travel)

What You'll Be Doing

Pipeline system engineering and design basis

Own the design basis for Nscale's gas transmission pipelines: hydraulic design, MAOP and pressure regime, line pack and inventory strategy, routing and sizing philosophy, and expansion provisions for future lines.
Perform and direct steady-state and transient hydraulic modeling of the pipeline systems, and own the models as living engineering assets that answer real operating questions: inventory swing, survival time on line pack, ramp response, and curtailment scenarios.
Demonstrate explicitly how the pipeline design basis supports downstream commitments: engine fleet demand and turndown, campus availability requirements, and the nominations-versus-consumption balance that governs system pressure.
Evaluate gas storage and supply resilience options, including line pack utilization, interconnect diversity, and cross-connection strategies between lines, with clear analysis of the risk each option carries.

Process and controls engineering

Own the overpressure protection philosophy across the pipeline systems: regulation, monitor, slam-shut, and relief selection, justified against reliability requirements, industry practice, and regulatory obligations rather than habit.
Define the control philosophy at interconnects, letdown stations, and plant interfaces: pressure versus flow control, control interactions with upstream operators' facilities, and the measurement and SCADA provisions needed to run the system on inventory.
Apply process safety discipline to the pipeline scope: lead and support HAZOPs and design reviews, own the closure of actions, and carry management of change through design and construction.
Engineer the interface into the plant fuel gas systems, coordinating conditioning, letdown, and protection philosophies so pipeline and plant behave as one system.

Regulatory compliance and integrity

Own compliance of the pipeline designs with 49 CFR Part 192 and the applicable ASME B31 codes, including the code boundaries between jurisdictional pipeline and plant piping.
Establish material, welding, and construction specifications, class location and MAOP documentation, and the records discipline that a traceable, verifiable, and complete basis requires.
Lay the foundation for integrity management: baseline assessment planning, pigging and inspection provisions, and mainline valve philosophy, including remote actuation and its treatment in availability analysis.
Support commissioning and first gas: purge and pack planning, energization of the measurement and control systems, and readiness reviews in partnership with the commissioning and startup organization.

Third-party technical management

Technically manage the engineering consultants supporting the pipeline scope: set the design basis they work to, review and challenge their deliverables, and integrate their output into a coherent whole.
Direct pipeline construction contractors on technical matters: specification compliance, field queries, deviation dispositions, and as-built reconciliation.
Own the technical interface with upstream pipeline operators and interconnect counterparties: metering station design, control coordination, nominations behavior, and the operating agreements' technical exhibits.
Hold third parties to disciplined engineering, testing, and documentation, and know when their standard answer is not good enough for this application.
Own the scope, schedule, and budget of third-party pipeline engineering: define consultant scopes of work, review and recommend change orders and addenda, and hold firms accountable to their commitments.

Standards and cross-functional leadership

Develop Nscale's engineering standards, specifications, and reference designs for gas pipelines, so each new line builds on the last instead of starting over.
Coordinate with generation engineering on fuel gas requirements, with permitting and land teams on routing and regulatory strategy, and with commercial teams on gas supply and transportation arrangements.
Build and lead the internal pipeline engineering function, directing specialist consultants today and hiring and developing a team as the portfolio scales.
Communicate complex pipeline and process issues clearly to project leadership and executives, with honest assessments of risk and readiness, and represent Nscale's pipeline scope in design basis alignment with EPC partners, upstream operators, and customers.

About You

15+ years of natural gas pipeline engineering experience across design, construction, and operations, with significant time in a lead or owner's engineer role on transmission systems, including senior accountability for the outcome of major transmission projects.
Deep hydraulic engineering capability, including transient modeling of gas transmission systems, and the judgment to translate model results into design and operating decisions.
Strong process engineering instincts: comfort with inventory-based system behavior, regulation and overpressure protection design, control philosophy development, and process safety methods such as HAZOP.
Working fluency with 49 CFR Part 192 and ASME B31.8, including MAOP determination, class location, and the code interfaces with plant piping under B31.1 or B31.3.
Hands-on experience with measurement and regulation stations, interconnects with major interstate pipelines, and the commercial mechanics of nominations and transportation that drive system behavior.
Experience taking pipeline scopes through construction, hydrotest, and first gas on major projects, and comfort in the field when systems misbehave.
Proven ability to direct engineering consultants and construction contractors, and to make technically defensible decisions under schedule pressure.
Demonstrated ability to own a scope independently and be delegated to with confidence: establishing the basis, setting the pace, and escalating with solutions rather than problems.
Proven ability to build standards, processes, and teams in a fast-scaling environment, including hiring and developing engineers.
Industry standing (code committee participation, technical society leadership, or equivalent) is a plus.
Bachelor's degree in Mechanical, Chemical, or Civil Engineering or a related field; PE license preferred.
Willing and able to travel to project sites, vendor facilities, and construction spreads regularly (typically 25%, higher during construction and commissioning campaigns).

What We Can Offer You

At Nscale, you'll find a collaborative, supportive, and innovative environment where your contributions spark real impact. We're building something extraordinary, and our people are driving it.

Highly competitive US compensation package (base + bonus + equity), with performance reviews every 12 months
Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage
401(k) retirement plan with company match
Generous PTO plus US federal holidays
A career-defining opportunity to be an early member of one of the fastest growing AI infrastructure companies in the world
A human-first approach: We treat you as humans first. Our flexible workplace trusts Nscalers to deliver, giving you the autonomy needed to get the job done.

Equal Opportunities Statement

At Nscale, we are committed to fostering an inclusive, diverse, and equitable workplace. We believe that a variety of perspectives enriches our work environment, and we encourage applications from candidates of all backgrounds, experiences, and abilities. We strongly encourage applications from people of colour, the LGBTQ+ community, people with disabilities, neurodivergent people, parents, carers, and people from lower socio-economic backgrounds. If there's anything we can do to accommodate your specific situation, please let us know.

The employee may be required to perform additional duties, tasks, and responsibilities as assigned by management, consistent with the skills and qualifications required for the role.
